result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers name the real cause: every line is 15px in the same navy, with only bold to tell lines apart. Both also catch the Select span and the hidden seat warning. A has a factual slip: it says the hyphens stand in for the word "to", but the route line literally uses "to". A also pads with 'what works' and 'limits' sections. B is tighter and accurate throughout, and it adds useful points: the seat warning doesn't say which fare it means, and the trip duration is left for the reader to work out. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly identify the flat hierarchy: one size, one color and near-identical weights. Both also cover the Select span and the hidden seat warning. A is tighter and adds sharp observations: the seat warning doesn't say which fare it covers, the trip duration is left for the reader to work out, and Helvetica has no fallback. B is accurate, and its contrast check holds up, but it is wordier. It also slightly contradicts itself: it first notes the times are already bold, then calls them 'buried' at body size. Its 'what works' and limits sections add little.
